challenge.better_approach: Considered refusing every shape lack, not only new ones. Migrated outcomes plans carry 'no claim' lacks by design until build-open judges them, so every decide on them would refuse. A before/after diff checks only what this decision changes.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That bounds.out entries that are paths are spelled as writes_to spells them. Prose entries ('every other component') match no path and are inert.
challenge.prior_art: plan_migration and judge_plan already call transitions._shape_lacks; this is the third caller. Grepped tickets/ and questions/ for 'out is out': only the orchestrator's message.
challenge.real_collision: 03b7e5d1a4c2 (T1) makes _shape_lacks refuse writes outside bounds.in. With T1 landed, the widening keeps decide clean; without T1 it is still recorded. They are independent, and either can land first.

answers.falsifier: Done when the three teeth hold and the 11 decide-calling proofs stay green. Wrong if a rehearsal must legitimately write into bounds.out.
answers.how: Before rehearsal.decide writes, _bounds_widened refuses a bounds.out write and returns the paths to add. Those are added and appended to the line's text. Then _shape_lacks runs before and after, and any new lack refuses the decision. A one-shot backfill widens 96c1 and f695 through the artifact door.
answers.traces_to: Law 4: decide was a second door into the plan that skipped the cast door's check; 96c1 and f695 crossed it with writes outside their bounds.
answers.what: A rehearse --decide refuses a write into bounds.out, widens bounds.in by name for a path in neither list, and refuses a plan the cast door's shape check would newly refuse.
